title: A Genetic Algorithm for the 20-Bit OneMax Problem
description: Evolve a population of 30 bit strings of length 20 using k=3 tournament selection, single-point crossover, bit-flip mutation, and elitism.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Seed `random`, set `TARGET_LEN = 20`, `POP = 30`, `GENS = 40`, and `P_MUT = 0.02`, and define `fitness(ind)` as `sum(ind)` and `random_ind()` as a list of 20 random bits.

Define the three genetic operators. `tournament(pop, k=3)` picks the fittest of 3 random individuals; `crossover(a, b)` splices `a[:cut]` and `b[cut:]` at a random cut point. `mutate(ind)` flips each bit `g` to `1 - g` with probability `P_MUT`.

Create the initial population of 30 random individuals. In each generation, find `best` and preserve `[best]` via elitism. Generate `POP - 1` new children by mutating the crossover of two tournament winners.
Look at lines 25-27: `elite = [best]` copies the highest-fitness individual into the next generation unchanged, while the list comprehension fills the remaining 29 slots.

steps.question: Because `elite = [best]` is always kept on line 25, can `fitness(max(pop, key=fitness))` ever decrease from one generation to the next?
steps.answer: No: the best individual from the current generation is copied unchanged into `pop` for the next generation, so the maximum fitness in `pop` is non-decreasing across generations.

steps.description: In generation 0, `max(pop, key=fitness)` finds the best initial bit string and prints `gen   0  best fitness = 14/20`.
Inside `crossover(a, b)` for the first child, line 15 slices `a[:cut] + b[cut:]` before `mutate` flips bits with probability `0.02`.
